subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser-specific public URL/domain/path denylist, or fold this request into a broader cross-tool egress/security policy?
rationale: This would become operator-facing security/config surface, and the open related issues show competing scopes that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design unified browser policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define deny/warn behavior for browser navigation, redirects, proxy-routed profiles, defaults, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Fold into generic egress policy
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685 canonical if maintainers want one policy for browser, web_fetch, web_search, and plugin HTTP egress.

options.title: Reject browser denylist surface
options.body: Close this and document hostname allowlist/private-network controls if maintainers decide bot-blocked public domains should remain an operator workflow concern outside OpenClaw config.

recommendation.title: Design unified browser policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define deny/warn behavior for browser navigation, redirects, proxy-routed profiles, defaults, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest browser SSRF/default-hardening history for the policy boundary this issue would extend.
